title: well, i’ll let you go by Bubba Weiler at Studio Seaview #wellillletyo...
transcript: Now in a new space but with the same quiet devastation that knocked me over the first time I saw it, “well, I'll let you go” is back for an encore run off-Broadway. Taking place in an ordinary Midwestern town, it follows a woman wading through her grief over her late husband whose death was both unexpected and circumstantially confusing. There's a bit of a mystery element that unfolds over the course of the play, but even setting aside the interesting and relatively understated plot, the acting and the direction here are phenomenal. Quincy Tyler Bernstine is fantastic in the central role, carrying a combination of familiar melancholy and relentless internal churn. While the show is a slow burn and certainly more sad than it is happy, I found it funnier than I remembered it being the first time around. Maybe it was the audience on the particular night that I attended, but I also feel like the new space and the more compressed staging gives the piece a slightly warmer tone. In any case, the beauty of this production is that while it's simple, it's been carefully constructed to ground a story that delivers a plethora of emotion, inviting every audience member to notice whatever aspects of the play feel most prominent to them. I love when something is kaleidoscopic like this, and in this case, it's a good play no matter how you turn it. With that, another program for my collection.
